[[Category:Mathematical modelling]]
A '''probabilistic model''' is a [[mathematical modelling|mathematical model]] in which outcomes cannot be determined before hand even if all identified conditions are known.

== Example ==

=== Coin flip ===

{{Hidden example}}
When modelling flipping a fair coin, one can assert the probability of a head on a given flip is always $\frac{1}{2}$, but one cannot assert if a particular flip will be head or tail.
{{End hidden}}
